back_translation: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, speak to your people and say to them: Suppose I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land take one man from among them and appoint him as their watchman,
and he sees the sword coming against the land and blows the ram's horn to warn the people.
If anyone hears the sound of the horn but does not heed the warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head.
He heard the sound of the horn but did not heed the warning; his blood is on himself. Had he heeded the warning, he would have saved his life.

But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the horn to warn the people, and the sword comes and takes a life, that person is taken away in his iniquity, but I will require his blood from the watchman's hand.
As for you, son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel; so when you hear a word from My mouth, warn them on My behalf.

When I say to the wicked, ‘O wicked man, you will surely die,’ but you do not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked man will die in his iniquity, but I will require his blood from your hand.
But if you warn the wicked to turn from his way, and he does not turn from it, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life.
As for you, son of man, say to the house of Israel: You say, ‘Our transgressions and our sins are upon us, and we are wasting away because of them; how can we live?’

Say to them: The Lord GOD says, As surely as I live, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn back! Turn back from your evil ways! Why will you die, O house of Israel?

As for you, son of man, say to your people: The righteousness of the righteous will not deliver him in the day of his transgression, and the wickedness of the wicked will not make him stumble in the day he turns from his wickedness; the righteous will not be able to live by his righteousness in the day he sins.

When I say to the righteous that he will surely live, but he then trusts in his righteousness and commits iniquity, none of his righteous deeds will be remembered; he will die for the iniquity he has done.
And when I say to the wicked, ‘You will surely die,’ but he turns from his sin and does what is just and right—
if the wicked restores the pledge, repays what he stole, and walks in the statutes of life, doing no iniquity—he will surely live; he will not die.
None of the sins he committed will be held against him. He has done what is just and right; he will surely live.
Yet your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ But it is their own way that is not just.
When the righteous turns from his righteousness and does iniquity, he will die for it.
And when the wicked turns from his wickedness and does what is just and right, he will live by it.
Yet you say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’ O house of Israel, I will judge each of you according to his ways.”
On the fifth day of the tenth month, in the twelfth year of our exile, a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me and said, “The city has fallen!”
The evening before the fugitive arrived, the hand of the LORD was upon me, and He opened my mouth before the man came to me in the morning. So my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, those who live in the ruins in the land of Israel are saying, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet he possessed the land; but we are many, so surely the land is given to us as a possession.’
Therefore say to them, the Lord GOD says this: You eat meat with the blood still in it, lift your eyes to your idols, and shed blood. Should you then possess the land?
You rely on your swords, you commit abominations, and each of you defiles his neighbor's wife. Should you then possess the land?

Say this to them, the Lord GOD says this: As surely as I live, those in the ruins will fall by the sword, those in the open field I will give as food to the beasts, and those in the strongholds and caves will die of pestilence.
I will make the land a desolate waste, and the pride of its strength will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will be desolate, so that no one passes through.
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I make the land a desolate waste because of all the abominations they have committed.
As for you, son of man, your people talk about you by the city walls and in the doorways of the houses, each saying to one another, ‘Come, let us hear the word that comes from the LORD.’

My people come to you as a crowd comes, and they sit before you as My people and hear your words, but they do not put them into practice. With their mouths they show love, but their hearts pursue dishonest gain.
Indeed, to them you are like a singer of love songs with a beautiful voice who plays skillfully. They hear your words but do not put them into practice.
When this comes—and it surely will—then they will know that a prophet has been among them.”
